style: Eastern Nagara / Gangetic hill temple architecture
key_structures: Hilltop Garbhagriha facing east with stone carvings
Flight of ancient rock-cut steps winding up Bhasmakuta hill
Mandapa with relief figures of Shiva and Ganesha
Akhanda Deepa (eternal lamp burning from antiquity)
Brahma Kund at the hill base
special_features: Sanctum houses an ancient uncarved natural stone manifestation symbolizing the maternal breast of Sati
Akhanda Jyoti (lamp burning uninterruptedly for centuries nourished with ghee)
Fine 15th-century bas-relief sculptures of Mahishasuramardini and Surya
renovation_history: Ancient sanctum referenced in Padma and Vayu Puranas; structural stone shrine erected around 15th century CE; expanded by local rulers and pilgrimage trusts.
